briefs.headline: Pochettino names 25 for Nations League quarterfinal with Haiti
briefs.summary: Pulisic, McKennie and Balogun return for the first time since the World Cup. The first leg is Nov. 14 in Miami, 4:30 p.m. ET; the second Nov. 17 at TQL Stadium, 7 p.m. ET, the U.S. men's national team's fourth visit there.

briefs.headline: Reds hire Guardians' Joe Torres as pitching coach
briefs.summary: Terry Francona's former Cleveland assistant inherits a staff that posted MLB's third-highest ERA, 4.83, in a last-place season of 75 wins and 87 losses; Chase Burns won 15 games for the Reds.

briefs.summary: Cole Palmer, with 14 caps and five goals in 11 Chelsea games this season, misses Croatia and Spain after Thomas Tuchel's "misses too many camps" warning; Jobe Bellingham gets a first senior call.

briefs.summary: Deshaun Watson is listed questionable with his concussion after missing practices; Shedeur Sanders, with three wins in seven rookie starts, has prepared for the Superdome. The Browns have been outscored 65 to 13 in first quarters.

briefs.headline: No kyujo in top two divisions as Kyushu basho opens Sunday
briefs.summary: The Japan Sumo Association's Friday scheduling meeting in Fukuoka listed no kyujo (absences) at juryo (second division) or above for the basho (tournament), Nov. 8 to 22; yokozuna Hoshoryu, out three tournaments after knee surgery, opens against Churanoumi, and Onosato draws Yoshinofuji, who has beaten him four times in five bouts.

briefs.headline: Wakatakakage back in juryo after four leg surgeries
briefs.summary: The May yusho (championship) winner, out two basho with compartment syndrome in his left leg, faces Ryuden on day 1 from juryo west No. 5; Nikkan Sports reported the surgeries ran to four and a delay could have cost the leg.

briefs.headline: Jaguars rout Ravens 33-10 as rookie Fagnano starts at QB
briefs.summary: Joe Fagnano went 10 of 18 for 60 yards with two interceptions as Baltimore (4-5) lost a fourth straight while awaiting Jacoby Brissett; Jacksonville (6-2) leads the AFC South by 3.5 games.

briefs.headline: Henry passes Tomlinson for seventh on all-time rushing list
briefs.summary: Taking Wildcat snaps for a quarterback-less Baltimore, Derrick Henry ran 17 times for 57 yards to reach 13,707, passing Jerome Bettis and LaDainian Tomlinson; Curtis Martin is next at 14,101.

briefs.headline: Warriors run streak to six with 20-point win over Heat
briefs.summary: Stephen Curry scored 29 and passed Oscar Robertson for 17th on the career list; Golden State has won six straight after opening with three losses. Klay Thompson had 11 for Miami in his return.

briefs.headline: Suns snap four-game skid with 13-point win over Magic
briefs.summary: Devin Booker scored 30 and Phoenix, with two wins in seven games, hit 17 of 34 threes; Orlando committed 25 turnovers, worth 36 Suns points, and has lost three straight.

briefs.headline: Ducks beat Oilers 5-4; Gauthier has nine goals in four games
briefs.summary: Cutter Gauthier is the first Anaheim player with nine goals in a four-game span; Edmonton (11-3-3) lost a second straight with fourth-string goalie Matt Tomkins in net.

briefs.headline: Canucks fall to 3-14-1 with a 6-2 loss in Winnipeg
briefs.summary: Dawson Mercer scored his first goal for Winnipeg (6-8-3) and six different Jets scored; Vancouver has three wins in 18 games this season.

briefs.headline: James Madison routs Southern Miss 54-23 as Evans returns
briefs.summary: JC Evans, in his first start since the opener, threw for 251 yards and ran for three touchdowns; the Dukes (8-2, 5-2 Sun Belt) ended a two-game skid.

briefs.headline: Bournemouth go 4 for 4 in Europe, 3-1 at Sparta Prague
briefs.summary: Tyler Adams equalised from outside the box in the 57th minute; Evanilson and Rayan finished it. The Cherries have 12 points from four Europa League games.

briefs.headline: Kamada's stoppage-time goal rescues Palace a 1-1 draw
briefs.summary: Alexander Prass put Hoffenheim ahead in the seventh minute at Selhurst Park; Daichi Kamada levelled in the 91st. Crystal Palace have five points from four Europa League games.

briefs.headline: Naylor testifies Clase and Ortiz pitches looked routine
briefs.summary: On day two of testimony in Brooklyn, former Guardians catcher Bo Naylor, a defense witness, called the flagged pitches common sliders low and away; a DraftKings investigator traced 160 account pings to Clase's house.

waters.reading: 56.2 cfs, 1.35 feet at 5:15 a.m., steady on both against 56.2 cfs and 1.35 feet in the fetcher's comparison.
waters.working: Against Thursday's edition reading of 54.9 cfs and 1.34 feet at 5:15 a.m. the gauge is up 1.3 cfs and 0.01 feet on the day, the first morning in 20 that is not down, after 19 straight falling mornings since the Oct. 17 crest. It is not a rise: for 48 hours the USGS trace has flickered between 54.9 and 56.2 cfs, one gauge increment, with the stage at 1.34 or 1.35, and 5:15 a.m. landed on the upper step, which has held since midnight. The daily means say where the recession went: 1,360 cfs on Oct. 15, 653 on Oct. 17, 141 on Oct. 24, 70.7 on Oct. 31, 65.0 on Nov. 1, 60.8, 57.7, 55.5 and 55.6 through Thursday, flattened to the gauge's resolution, with no rain signal anywhere on the trace. The read string is the fetcher's own verdict, printed as it stands, "56 cfs - prime wading water." Stocking: WVDNR's fish-stocking page, fetched this morning, carries an empty list under the waters stocked, and no November report names the Williams, the Cranberry or the Summersville tailwater; the river's most recent stocking this paper has reported is still Oct. 29. At 56 cfs and clear the Williams is as low as it has been since the Oct. 15 freshet and fishes as the file's low-water problem: pocket water and plunge pools shrunk to their cores, every fish in the deepest slot of each pocket, the water cold and glass-clear, and a wading angler the loudest thing on the river. Structure is pocket water, plunge pools and undercut banks; forage is caddis, stoneflies and sculpin. So: a long leader, nine to 12 feet to 6X or 7X, and small flies, a size 16 to 18 caddis pupa or a size 18 soft-hackle swung into the plunge-pool tailouts, a size 16 to 18 pheasant tail or small black stonefly nymph under a tiny indicator or a dry-dropper through the pocket seams, a size 20 to 22 blue-winged olive on top through the middle of an overcast day, and for the one bigger fish in each plunge pool a size 8 to 10 olive or black sculpin pattern fished on a short line into the foam at the head of the pool at first or last light, before the sun gets on it; an egg pattern or a San Juan worm under a small indicator still covers the holdover stocked pools. The heavy-nymph-on-the-seam game is for 500 cfs, and the trace shows nothing like it coming.

waters.read: 25.0 ft — normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: The fetcher reads the pool steady, 0.04 under its 25.06 comparison point, but against Thursday's edition reading of 24.44 at 5 a.m. the pool is up 0.58 on the day. Thursday's trace bottomed at 24.27 at 9 a.m., then climbed all day, 24.48 at 2 p.m., 24.80 at 6 p.m., 25.08 at 11 p.m., and held between 24.97 and 25.03 overnight: the pool drawn down 0.6 feet Wednesday night was refilled through Thursday daytime, with no rain in the bucket, so the water came back through the dam, not off the hills. The read string is the fetcher's band verdict, normal pool, ordinary bank access, and at 25.0 the gauge is two feet under the up-and-pushing line at 27. A pool back up half a foot and clear fishes the structure, not the slack: wing dams, riprap and the lock wall are the file's structure, shad and skipjack with crawfish in the rock the forage. A white or pearl three-and-a-half to four-inch swimbait on a half-ounce head or a three-quarter-ounce spoon down the current face of each wing dam at first light for hybrids and white bass; a crawfish-colored jig or a three-inch tube dragged slow on the riprap through the day for smallmouth and drum; and with the water cooling into November a half-ounce blade bait or a jig and minnow worked vertical along the lock wall seam and the barge-cut edges for sauger, cut skipjack on the bottom in the cuts after dark for blue catfish. With the pool refilled there is a little less pull through it than Thursday, so everything slows down a notch.

waters.near: below R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.reading: 26.17 feet at 5 a.m., steady against 26.02 in the fetcher's comparison.
waters.read: 26.2 ft — normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: The fetcher reads the gauge steady, 0.15 over its 26.02 comparison point; against Thursday's edition reading of 26.29 at 5 a.m. it is down 0.12 on the day, and the day itself was a round trip: the trace fell from 26.32 at 6 a.m. Thursday to a 25.61 low at 8:30 p.m., then came back up overnight, 25.98 at midnight, 26.06 at 2 a.m., 26.16 at 3:30 a.m., 26.17 at 5 a.m., up 0.56 in eight and a half hours while Point Pleasant held flat. The dam below tells the rest: the USGS gauge at Ironton, Ohio, below Greenup Dam, recorded Greenup's discharge falling from 29,300 cfs at 6 a.m. Thursday to 13,900 between 7:30 and 8:15 p.m., then back to 18,300 to 21,400 through the night and 20,300 at 4:30 a.m., the Ironton stage 34.51, 33.98 and 34.39 at the same points. So the overnight pool transfer this paper watched three nights of four did not repeat in that form: Thursday the Byrd pool was refilled by day while the Huntington reach drained 0.7 and Greenup cut its release by more than half, and overnight Huntington recovered 0.56 with the pool above flat. Whether it is scheduled or a lockage pattern the traces still do not say, and this paper will not guess. The read string is the fetcher's band verdict, normal pool, ordinary bank access. Below the dam the reach came up half a foot overnight, so there is fresh push on the seams this morning with Greenup passing about 20,000 cfs below, and the fishing goes to them: a white swimbait or a three-quarter-ounce spoon down the current face of the wing dams at first light for hybrids and white bass, a half-ounce blade bait or a chartreuse-and-white paddletail on a half-ounce head worked slow along the lock wall's downstream edge for sauger, which feed better with the push on, a crawfish jig on the riprap at midday, and cut skipjack on the bottom in the slack beside the discharge after dark for blue and flathead catfish. No color in either trace; the slack-behind-the-dams game is for a muddy river, not this one.

waters.reading: Sound at Hampstead: high 5:32 AM at 4.1 ft, low 12:02 PM at 0.6 ft, high 5:49 PM at 3.6 ft, low 12:14 AM (Sat) at 0.3 ft. Surf at Ocean City Beach pier: high 4:55 AM at 5.2 ft, low 11:10 AM at 0.4 ft, high 5:11 PM at 4.4 ft, low 11:09 PM at 0.2 ft. Water 67.5F at Beaufort, 60 miles up the coast, observed 5:30 a.m. Moon a waning crescent, 13% illuminated, 26.1 days old.
waters.read: Fish the moving water either side of high at 5:32 AM and 5:49 PM in the sound.
waters.working: The sound lags the surf 37 minutes on the morning high, 52 on the midday low, 38 on the evening high and 65 on the late low, the long-lag-on-the-ebb pattern the reference describes. The ranges are building: a 3.5-foot drain this morning from 4.1 to 0.6, a 3.0-foot fill to 5:49 p.m., a 3.3-foot drain tonight, the morning sound high 4.1 against Thursday's 3.9 and the surf high 5.2 against 4.9, with the new moon about three days off and spring tides coming on. The water at Beaufort, 60 miles up the coast, reads 67.5F, up 0.9 on Thursday's 66.6, a third straight morning of warming. What's running: the Fisherman's Post Topsail and Sneads Ferry report for November, published Sunday, Nov. 1, is five days old this morning, a monthly report and not today's conditions. It has the Jolly Roger Pier with scattered speckled trout showing, night bottom fishing producing Virginia mullet and spot, and bluefish thick in the early mornings; Surf City Pier with pompano, black drum and croakers on the bottom, casting shots at Spanish and bluefish, and king mackerel good before the last blow; East Coast Sports with the piers catching a few red drum of 32 inches and more, mostly on the north end, smaller reds and the occasional trout inside, and trout to dominate as it cools; Native Son with the cooling water pushing trout into the creeks, the deeper seams of five to eight feet the place to look, and reds inside taking cut bait over artificials; Capt. Ricky Kellum with many small specks and some to 28 inches on live shrimp under a cork in four to eight feet of water on structure and current, black drum to 18 inches and small reds on floated shrimp; Carolina Flats with topwater early to find the trout schools, deeper holes later, and reds on the oyster bars and grass banks on soft plastics; and the boats with kings in 50 to 60 feet, bluefish, false albacore and gray trout on the nearshore structure, sea bass and triggerfish on the bottom in 60 to 80 feet. Beach conditions: no NWS Wilmington product was active for coastal Pender or Onslow or the adjacent marine zones at 5:48 a.m. Tide is the whole game, and this morning it starts at press time: the sound topped out at 5:32 a.m. and is beginning its drain to the 12:02 p.m. low, the biggest morning ebb of the week. Structure here is oyster bars, grass edges, dock lights and the ICWW channel, forage mud minnows, shrimp and finger mullet, which is the report's live-shrimp-and-small-plastic fishing. Trout first: a topwater plug over the grass edges in the first hour of light with the ebb just moving, then a 3/16- or quarter-ounce jighead with a paddletail or soft jerkbait worked slow down the five- to eight-foot seams where the creek channels drop into the ICWW as the drain gathers through mid-morning, and a popping cork with live shrimp over the oyster bars on the first of the flood after noon and again either side of the 5:49 p.m. high. Red drum want the last of the fall, which comes twice today, roughly 9:30 a.m. to the 12:02 p.m. low and after dark from about 9:45 p.m. to the 12:14 a.m. low, cut menhaden or a finger mullet on a quarter-ounce head a couple of feet off the creek-channel edges as the grass drains; the dusk high puts drum on the flooded grass and oyster banks for a weedless gold spoon or a soft plastic. Spot and sea mullet on bloodworm or shrimp on a two-hook bottom rig in the ICWW channel an hour either side of the evening high, and under the dock lights on tonight's ebb the same small plastics or a suspending twitchbait where the shrimp and finger mullet stack. Bluefish are the early-morning fish on the beach behind the bait pods on a metal jig or topwater, per both piers. Flounder are release only under FF-27-2026.
